name: bronze_packing
description: a circle packing in bronze and gold: the frame filled with round discs of every size, each a flat metal disc with a dark bevel, a bright rim, a glint at its centre, faint rays and a packing of smaller beads inside, glints crowding the cusps where discs meet, and the set's own components gold star-flowers among them

reference.made_with: unknown; a Kleinian/inversion circle packing, 3840x2160 (a 4k desktop background, the sibling of teal_tunnel's reference)

reuses: the style compositor, its palette, light, glow and sheet layers, warp, invert, and the normal, multiply, add and screen blends
field smooth through the map by rank: the escaped field no disc caught
the inside channel by rank at gamma 0.6: the set's components as gold flowers, their rings of convergence the petals
the light layer at period 2 on the new bubble height: each disc a shallow dome (rings 0.4) with a Fresnel rim and a specular highlight
the glow layer four times on the bubble height: a multiplied dark bevel inside each rim, the bright rim itself, a glint at each disc's centre, and the same rim and glint on the nested discs
a glow on the entry step: the late, tiny discs that crowd every cusp, lit as sparkle
a sheet on the entry angle at six bands: faint rays from each disc's centre
the tone pass, at the reference's median and p10
adds: channel bubble {center, radius, hit, read, spacing, escaped, largest}: the disc |z - center| < radius read at the step the orbit enters it for the hit-th time, its own loop with dz kept so the height has a gradient. The samples entering first at step n are a conformal preimage of the disc, so they draw round discs, and later steps fill the gaps: a circle packing. read is height (1 - |z - center|/radius, a dome a light at period 2 lights as a hemisphere), step (one number per disc) or angle (rays from each disc's middle); hit 2 is a packing of smaller discs inside each disc of hit 1; spacing repeats the disc on a square lattice so almost every orbit lands in one; escaped reads only escaping orbits, leaving the set's components to the inside channel; largest passes over an entry whose disc pulls back larger than that fraction of the frame width (radius / |dz| > largest * width), so the packing starts at a frame-relative size at any zoom depth

knobs.name: disc_size
knobs.label: Bubble size
knobs.what: the largest bubble, as a share of the frame width; smaller packs more, finer bubbles

knobs.name: shine
knobs.label: Metal shine
knobs.what: how bright the specular glint on each disc's dome is

knobs.name: rim_glow
knobs.label: Rim glow
knobs.what: the bright metallic ring round every disc

knobs.name: star_rays
knobs.label: Star rays
knobs.what: the six-pointed star cut into each disc

notes: Lessons: The fifth style came from a circle packing (most likely an inversion or Kleinian render, not escape-time), and its circles went in as one channel, the bubble trap: the existing circle trap keeps the orbit's closest pass to a circle, which draws rings that cross, where a packing needs **discs read at an entry**. Everything else — the dome, the bevel, the rim, the glint, the rays, the nested beads, the cusp sparkle — is the old layers on the channel's three reads. Three lessons. **One disc is a target most orbits miss; a lattice of discs is one every orbit hits**, and that is the difference between a few bubbles on the set and a frame packed with them. **A disc holding a critical point pulls back as a peanut**, so the lattice is offset off `0`, and a disc holding an attracting cycle smears a whole component, so the trap reads escaping orbits only and leaves the inside to the `inside` channel. **A gallery location is a deep zoom**, where every early disc pulls back far larger than the frame and crosses it as straight bands; bounding the disc size as a fraction of the frame (`largest`) is what makes the style stand at every location instead of at hand-placed shallow ones. And one about the tone check: this style's sub-pixel beads average up at supersample 2, so while the tone pass measured the samples, the frame's p10 at full resolution sat ~0.05–0.07 above its target, and the stack's `p10` was hand-lowered to 0.05 to land in the band. That gap is why the pass now measures the averaged picture: the stack holds the reference's own 0.099, and its picture reads p10 0.100 at both 1280x800 and 2560x1600; `style tones`' 640-wide copy reads 0.13–0.14, in band.
